第 50 章 Making Your New Team Feel Like a Team让你的新团队感觉像个团队

Camille Fournier / 卡米尔·福尼耶

— 第 147 页 —

Engineering is a team sport. Gone are the days of the lone software developer churning out code alone in their room. In most effective organizations, software is written by engineers who are acting in teams. We work in shared codebases, give each other code reviews, and even sometimes write code in pairs. Good managers of software teams understand that it is their job to create this collaborative environment. It's not enough to focus on one-on-one meetings and understanding people as individuals, you also must work with the team as a whole to make the group effective.

工程是团队运动。孤独的软件开发者在房间里独自写代码的日子已经过去。在大多数高效组织中，软件是工程师以团队形式写的。我们在共享代码库中工作、互相做代码评审、甚至有时候结对写代码。好的软件团队经理明白创造这种协作环境是他们的工作。只关注一对一会议和把人作为个体理解是不够的，你还必须和团队整体合作让团队有效。

Learning how to do this takes time, and it is just as awkward to start as your early one-on-ones might feel. Here are some questions to answer as you begin:

学习怎么做这件事需要时间，开始时可能和你早期一对一一样尴尬。以下是你开始时要回答的一些问题：

  • What is your team called? Naming is one of the most difficult problems in computer science, and spending some time on the name you give your team is a good thing to do. It forces you to succinctly describe the work that your team does, so try to resist the urge to name your team by obscure analogy. It's better to call yourself the Sales Engineering team rather than Team Glengarry.你的团队叫什么？命名是计算机科学最难的问题之一，花时间给团队起名是好事。它迫使你简洁描述团队做的工作，所以尽量忍住用晦涩类比给团队起名的冲动。叫自己销售工程团队比叫 Glengarry 团队好。
— 第 148 页 —

Naming is the first step in the long-running project of defining your team's mission.

命名是定义团队使命这个长期项目的第一步。

What are the processes that your team does together, as a group? You might follow some variant of an Agile methodology, which gives you an automatic baseline for bringing the team together to work. If you don't, you need to bring your team together regularly to discuss the work! If you're at a loss, I would recommend a regular quick standup meeting for briefly reviewing in-flight work and priorities, and periodic retrospectives to look back and talk about what went well and what could improve. No matter what you do, it is important that you bring your team together as a group to talk about the work on a regular cadence.

你们团队作为一个群体一起做什么流程？你可能遵循某种敏捷方法论的变体，这给你自动的基线让团队一起工作。如果没有，你需要定期把团队聚在一起讨论工作！如果你不知所措，我建议定期快速站会简要评审在途工作和优先级，以及定期回顾会回顾什么做得好、什么可以改进。无论你做什么，重要的是你定期把团队作为群体聚在一起讨论工作。

Think about the roles that each team member plays with respect to the team as a whole. One person is the operations expert, whereas another is the architect. Jane is seen as the technical leader; Joe is the junior engineer. Where do the responsibilities of these roles overlap, and where are there gaps? You might discover that you need to hire for missing capabilities or cross-train people to ensure good coverage of important skills.

想想每个团队成员相对于团队整体扮演什么角色。一个人是运维专家，另一个是架构师。Jane 被视为技术领导；Joe 是初级工程师。这些角色的责任在哪里重叠、哪里有缺口？你可能发现需要为缺失的能力招人或交叉培训人员以确保重要技能覆盖良好。

How are you making sure that there is good knowledge sharing across members of the team? Code reviews are rarely enough. Consider having team members share their work by presenting it to the group, writing and discussing their designs, and sharing support responsibilities broadly.

你怎么确保团队成员之间有良好的知识共享？代码评审很少够。考虑让团队成员通过向群体展示、写和讨论设计、广泛共享支持责任来分享他们的工作。

Two things will begin to happen when you think about the team as a group. The first is that you'll be forced to pay attention to how your team works together. If there are two members who cannot work together, that is something that you must address. On a team of 10 or fewer people, having two people who are in deep conflict is a problem for the team's health and something you need to take seriously.

当你把团队作为群体思考时，两件事会开始发生。第一是你会被迫注意团队怎么一起工作。如果有两个成员不能一起工作，这是你必须解决的事情。在 10 人或更少的团队中，有两个人深度冲突是团队健康的问题，你需要认真对待。

— 第 149 页 —

The second is that you'll begin to see that the way your team works together contributes greatly to the happiness of its members. Thinking of the team as a system itself instead of just a grouping of individuals can help you avoid one of the common early management traps, which is micro-optimizing for individual happiness over the strength of the team. Individual engineers don't always know what will make them happy and often overvalue the things they can easily understand, like hard technical challenges or promotions. Your job is to make sure the team doesn't neglect things that are more difficult to understand but cause longer-term happiness, like being able to release their code frequently.

第二是你会开始看到团队一起工作的方式极大地影响成员的幸福感。把团队本身看作一个系统而不只是个人的组合，可以帮你避免常见的早期管理陷阱之一——为了个人幸福微观优化而牺牲团队实力。个体工程师并不总是知道什么会让他们幸福，往往高估他们容易理解的事情，比如困难的技术挑战或晋升。你的工作是确保团队不忽视那些更难理解但带来更长期幸福的事情，比如能够频繁发布代码。

This transition to thinking beyond individuals and about the team as a whole is stressful. There can be a lag between making changes that benefit the entire team and seeing the value of those changes. The first time you need to disappoint an individual in favor of the team's overall needs is tough. For the long-term well-being of the group, it is critical that you think about the team as your first order of business. So, give it a name, make sure it meets regularly, and get everyone working together, and you'll be on the road to a high-performing team.

这种超越个人、把团队作为整体思考的转变是有压力的。在做出惠及整个团队的改变和看到这些改变的价值之间可能有滞后。第一次你需要为了团队整体需求让个人失望时是艰难的。为了群体的长期福祉，把团队作为首要事务来思考至关重要。所以，给它起个名字、确保它定期开会、让每个人一起工作，你就走在通往高绩效团队的路上。
